title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 11/27 — "At the Window"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 11. Home again, soaked and emptied out, the narrator climbs to his study without knowing why. The window stands open, and the whole country towards Horsell is on fire: a wrecked train burning on the railway, the houses about Woking station glowing as ruins, and across the red light, huge black shapes moving busily to and fro.

He sits and stares until, near dawn, a soldier comes over the garden palings. He is a driver in the artillery, hatless, his face black with smoke, and he has seen the army on the common wiped out in minutes. In the dark dining room, with no lamp lit for fear of the Martians, he drinks the whisky, puts his head on his arms, and weeps like a little boy.

At first light the two of them look out again. The valley has become a valley of ashes, and three of the metallic giants stand about the pit, their cowls turning as though surveying what they have made.

Chapter XI of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
